label: 0054 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 53 windows): 0053 with the Japan Trench megathrust as the base of the elastic forearc after Tohoku (slip deficit beyond coupling 1 in a state of its own, with its own decay), uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0053 plus a second Tohoku state on the Japan Trench megathrust. It can only add slip deficit, is left out of the cap at coupling 1, and decays on its own clock (one pattern, Omori with c = 1 yr). In the BEL framework of Loveless and Meade (2025), the megathrust is the base of the elastic upper plate beneath the offshore forearc. Slip deficit beyond the plate rate there is a displacement condition on that base: what relaxation below the forearc, or a slab moving faster than the plate, does to it. Coupling off Miyagi at 0–20 km is about −5 in the first month after Tohoku (afterslip), 2–3 through 2011, about 1.5 by 2014 and 1.1 by 2019; 0052's first-week value of 54 is gone. The coupling drawn is the total. Off Iwate and Ibaraki at 20–40 km the deficit state and the afterslip offset each other, and only their sum is constrained. Seafloor residuals beneath the Japan Trench after Tohoku are 28 and 48 mm, as in 0052. Held-out seafloor sites are predicted better than by 0052 (cross-validation +1,138 against the trench state without seafloor-driven deficit; 0052 +916, 0053 +109), and so are held-out onshore windows (+548; 0052 −416, 0053 −651). It is the best of the three BEL configurations tested (0054–0056). Seafloor data: Japan Coast Guard (CC BY-NC 4.0) and Tohoku University (CC BY 4.0).
